study.title: S-MEOD: A Novel Evaluation Metric for Frame-Based Medical Object Detection
study.venue: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine

imaging.modality_detail: Coronary X-ray angiography frames (public Danilov et al. stenosis dataset), acquired on Coroscop (Siemens) and Innova (GE Healthcare)
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries, one-vessel coronary artery disease, stenosis detection
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 14-75 frames per validation video; evaluated in fixed 5-frame sequences

public_dataset_used.detail: Danilov et al. angiographic dataset for stenosis detection (Mendeley Data, doi 10.17632/ydrm75xywg.2)

data_released.detail: Datasets analyzed available from the corresponding author on reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Informative frames selected by interventional cardiologists; bounding boxes annotated with LabelBox (from source dataset)

task.task_description: Proposes S-MEOD, a sequence-level evaluation metric (combining Sequence-aware Precision and Sequence-oriented Detection over fixed 5-frame sequences) for frame-based medical object detection, demonstrated on YOLOv10x coronary stenosis detection across confidence thresholds.
task.clinical_application: Evaluation of AI-assisted coronary artery stenosis detection in angiography sequences

temporal_evidence.quote: in frame-based data, an object detection model may detect true positives in just a few frames

G1.quote: challenges like low resolution of medical imaging and limited availability of valid datasets pose significant obstacles in some research areas

G2.quote: its behavior in other domains or imaging modalities requires further investigation

G3.quote: Existing metrics do not explicitly account for temporal structure across frames, which limits their suitability for frame-based medical imaging tasks

G6.quote: future work will include expert reader studies to quantitatively assess how S-MEOD correlates with human diagnostic judgment

G9.quote: Issues such as unbalanced annotated datasets, reliability concerns, and the inherent diversity of medical imaging modalities

other_limitations: S-MEOD does not directly improve detection performance
Should be used alongside conventional metrics when dense frame-by-frame accuracy is critical
Validated on a single dataset and single medical imaging task
future_work: Expert reader studies correlating S-MEOD with human diagnostic judgment
Applying S-MEOD to frame-based detection beyond the medical domain (defense, surveillance, remote sensing, disaster response, industrial inspection)
